query_ground_truth.workflow_task: Retrieve Trello card comments, update Trello cards, and perform broader project-management and automation-maintenance operations across task boards, email, chat, and an automation platform.
query_ground_truth.intent: Communicate updates and handle notifications through email and chat platforms.

results.execution_guidance: IMPORTANT: Follow the recommended plan below. Extract steps before execution, adapt to your current context, execute sequentially with current_step parameter, and check known pitfalls to avoid errors.
recommended_plan_steps: Required [Prerequisite]: Confirm intent and content before calling OUTLOOK_SEND_EMAIL and MICROSOFT_TEAMS_TEAMS_POST_CHAT_MESSAGE (both are irreversible writes).
Optional (if email deliverability is uncertain) [Prerequisite]: Check recipient constraints using OUTLOOK_GET_MAIL_TIPS (avoid known blocks before sending).

Optional (if chat target is unknown) [Prerequisite]: Resolve participants using MICROSOFT_TEAMS_LIST_USERS, then create or reuse a chat using MICROSOFT_TEAMS_TEAMS_CREATE_CHAT (store returned chat identifier).
Required [Step]: Send the email using OUTLOOK_SEND_EMAIL (use the supported "to" field; set is_html when body is HTML).
Required [Step]: Post the chat message using MICROSOFT_TEAMS_TEAMS_POST_CHAT_MESSAGE (ensure non-empty content; set content_type to match text vs HTML).
Optional (if review/approval is needed) [Fallback]: Create a draft using OUTLOOK_CREATE_DRAFT, then send it using OUTLOOK_SEND_DRAFT instead of sending immediately.
known_pitfalls: [OUTLOOK_SEND_EMAIL] May return HTTP 202 with an empty body; treat 202 as accepted/success rather than expecting a message payload.
[OUTLOOK_SEND_EMAIL] Uses the parameter name "to"; relying on alternate field names can fail or drop recipients.
[MICROSOFT_TEAMS_TEAMS_POST_CHAT_MESSAGE] content must be non-empty and content_type must match the format (text vs html) or rendering will be incorrect.
[MICROSOFT_TEAMS_TEAMS_POST_CHAT_MESSAGE] webUrl/deep link may be null in the response; don’t depend on it for navigation.

OUTLOOK_SEND_EMAIL.description: Sends an email with subject, body, recipients, and optional attachments via Microsoft Graph API. Supports comma-separated email addresses in the to_email field for multiple recipients. Accepts either a single file or a list of files as attachments. Attachments require a non-empty file with valid name and mimetype.

to.description: The primary recipient's email address(es). You can provide a single email or multiple emails separated by commas. Valid email addresses will be extracted from strings containing extra text. Format: name@domain.com

examples: Hello team, please find the attached report.
body.description: The content of the email body as a plain string (plain text or HTML based on `is_html`). Do not pass structured objects; provide only the raw text/HTML content.

is_html.description: Specifies if the email body is HTML; `True` for HTML, `False` for plain text.

subject.description: The subject line of the email.

to_name.description: The display name of the primary recipient.

user_id.description: The user's email address or the alias 'me' to represent the authenticated user.

cc_emails.description: List of email addresses for CC recipients. Each email should be a separate string in the array. Do NOT pass comma-separated values as a single string.

name.title: Name
name.description: The filename that will be used when uploading the file to the destination service

s3key.title: S3Key
s3key.description: The S3 key of a publicly accessible file, typically returned from a previous download action that stored the file in S3. This key references an existing file that can be uploaded to another service.

mimetype.title: Mimetype
mimetype.description: The MIME type of the file

from_address.description: Optional From address to set on the message (send as/on behalf). Provide a single email address. Requires appropriate mailbox permissions.

save_to_sent_items.description: Indicates if the email should be saved in 'Sent Items'.

MICROSOFT_TEAMS_TEAMS_POST_CHAT_MESSAGE.description: Sends a non-empty message (text or HTML) to a specified, existing Microsoft Teams chat; content must be valid HTML if `content_type` is 'html'.

locale.description: Locale of the chat message. Microsoft Teams currently documents this as client-set and always 'en-us'; only 'en-us' is supported.

chat_id.description: Unique identifier for the Microsoft Teams chat to receive the message.

examples:
Hello

This is a test message with HTML.
content.description: Message content, either plain text or HTML (see `content_type`).

subject.description: The subject of the chat message, in plaintext.

id.description: Index of an entity being mentioned in the specified chatMessage. Matches the {index} value in the corresponding <at id="{index}"> tag in the message body.
Unique identifier for the identity or actor.

displayName.description: The display name of the identity.

tag.description: If present, represents a tag @mentioned in a message.

id.description: Unique identifier for the identity or actor.

displayName.description: The display name of the identity.

user.description: If present, represents a user @mentioned in a message.

id.description: Unique identifier for the identity or actor.

displayName.description: The display name of the identity.

device.description: Not used because it's not supported to @mention devices.

id.description: Unique identifier for the identity or actor.

displayName.description: The display name of the identity.

application.description: If present, represents an application (for example, bot) @mentioned in a message.

conversationIdentityType.description: Type of conversation. Possible values are: team, channel, chat, unknownFutureValue.

conversation.description: If present, represents a conversation (for example, team, channel, or chat) @mentioned in a message.

mentioned.description: The entity (user, application, team, channel, or chat) that was @mentioned.

mentionText.description: String used to represent the mention. For example, a user's display name, a team name.

mentions.description: List of entities mentioned in the chat message. Supported entities are: user, bot, team, channel, chat, and tag.

importance.description: The importance of the chat message. Possible values: 'normal', 'high', 'urgent'. Defaults to 'normal' if not specified.

id.description: Read-only. The unique ID of the attachment.

content.description: The content of the attachment. If the attachment is a rich card, set the property to the rich card object. This property and contentUrl are mutually exclusive.

contentUrl.description: The URL for the content of the attachment. Mutually exclusive with content.

teamsAppId.description: The ID of the Teams app that is associated with the attachment. The property is used to attribute a Teams message card to the specified app.

contentType.description: The media type of the content attachment. It can have the following values: reference, file, forwardedMessageReference, or specialized content types like application/vnd.microsoft.card.codesnippet.

thumbnailUrl.description: The URL to a thumbnail image that the channel can use if it supports using an alternative, smaller form of content or contentUrl.

attachments.description: References to attached objects like files, tabs, meetings, or cards.

id.description: Read-only. Represents the chat message hosted content identifier.

contentType.description: Write-only. When posting new chat message hosted content, represents the type of content, such as image/png.

contentBytes.description: Write-only. When posting new chat message hosted content, represents the bytes of the payload. These are represented as a base64Encoded string.

microsoft_graph_temporary_id.description: Write-only. Represents the temporaryId for the hosted content while posting a message to refer to the hosted content in chatMessage resource being sent.

hostedContents.description: Content in a message hosted by Microsoft Teams - for example, inline images or code snippets.

MICROSOFT_TEAMS_LIST_USERS.description: Tool to list all users in the organization. Use when you need to retrieve directory users with filtering, pagination, and field selection.

top.description: Maximum number of users to return per page (1-999). Default is 100. For pages beyond the first, pass the `next_page_token` from the response back as `page_token`. Note: Some tenants have restrictive page size policies that may reject explicit $top values. If such an error occurs, the request will be retried without $top.

count.description: When true, include @odata.count in the response by sending $count=true. Microsoft Graph requires ConsistencyLevel: eventual for this advanced directory query.

filter.description: OData filter to refine results by property values (e.g., startswith(displayName,'A')).

search.description: OData search query for advanced text search across user properties. Requires ConsistencyLevel: eventual header. Use double quotes for phrases (e.g., "displayName:John"). Not available in Azure AD B2C tenants.

select.description: Comma-separated list of user properties to include (e.g., id,displayName,mail).

orderby.description: OData orderby clause to sort results (e.g., displayName desc). When combined with $filter, advanced query capabilities (ConsistencyLevel: eventual header and $count=true) may be required and will be added automatically if needed.

page_token.description: Opaque continuation token for the next page. Omit for the first page; then pass back the `next_page_token` from the previous response, unmodified, until it is absent. Do not construct or edit it. When set, it drives pagination; filter/sort/search params need not be repeated — the token carries them.

consistencyLevel.description: Set to 'eventual' when using advanced queries with $count or $search.
